summary: South Australia carries no region-specific statute, incident series or enforcement pattern in the country dossier, which lists it among the units with no sub-national signal — national criminal law and the national framework apply as written. The one operational fact that still differs from some neighbours: custody placement is not on the explicit self-identification basis used by NSW, Victoria, the ACT and Tasmania, so in South Australia a detained trans woman's placement depends on surgical-intervention status or case-by-case assessment. Neither a protective nor a hostile state-level campaign is documented.
